chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about urine that comes upon the body. He said, “Pour water over it twice, for it is only water.”
And I asked him about a garment that urine comes upon. He said, “Wash it twice.”
And I asked him about a young boy urinating on the garment. He said, “Pour a little water over it, then wring it out.”

key_terms.اَلثَّوْبِ: garment; the clothing item to be purified
key_terms.اَلصَّبِيِّ: young boy; the child whose urine on a garment is addressed here
key_terms.اَلْبَوْلِ: urine; the substance discussed as causing ritual impurity
key_terms.اَلْجَسَدَ: the body; the physical person upon whom urine may fall
key_terms.اَلْمَاءَ: water; the purifying agent used for cleansing
key_terms.تَعْصِرُهُ: you wring it out; squeezing the garment after pouring water on it
key_terms.مَرَّتَيْنِ: twice; the required number of washings mentioned in the ruling

ai.seo_question: How should the body and clothing be purified if urine comes upon them according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings on purifying the body and clothing from urine. It states that urine on the body is purified by pouring water twice, urine on a garment is washed twice, and when a young boy urinates on a garment, a little water is poured over it and then it is wrung out. The narration is significant in the fiqh of taharah and najasah.
